# Source scanner review — September 28, 2026

The catalog's HOL Plugin Scanner 3.0.123 result was reproduced against an
export of the native workspace's committed source: 71/100, six high findings.
This review targets useful source improvements, not admission-score changes.

## Findings and decisions

- `bin/lattices-action.ts`: interpolated app, plist, mount, and download paths
  were passed through a shell. Replace these calls with argument arrays. This
  fixes paths containing apostrophes and avoids interpreting path text as commands.
- `bin/lattices-app.ts`: apply the same treatment to resource copies, DMG
  mounting, bundle installation, timestamp updates, and signature inspection.
  Read `codesign` metadata from stderr explicitly and reject unsuccessful results.
- `bin/lattices.ts`: pass tmux targets and the detected package manager's build
  arguments directly. Generated session names and package managers are already
  constrained; this removes unnecessary shell interpretation rather than proving
  an externally exploitable bug in those paths.
- `products/action/native/engine/scripts/moondream-verify-screenshot.py`:
  `model.eval()` changes the model's training/evaluation state. It is not Python's
  built-in `eval`. Three of the six high findings repeat this same false positive
  across detected plugin surfaces. Keep the correct model API call unchanged.
- `.github/workflows`: pin external actions to verified upstream commit SHAs,
  default token permissions to read-only, scope write permissions to relevant
  jobs, and retain checkout credentials only for requested tag publication.

The CLI regressions run under `bun run test:cli`. They exercise literal paths
containing shell syntax, app copying, mount cleanup, signature metadata on stderr,
and tmux argument boundaries without installing or launching either app.

## Local validation

- `bun run check:types` passed.
- `bun run test:cli` passed: 42 tests passed, one daemon-down test skipped because
  the daemon was running. This includes five new subprocess regressions.
- `actionlint -shellcheck= -pyflakes=` and `git diff --check` passed.
- A second local scan of the exported source with both workspaces' changes
  overlaid reports 73/100, three high and eight medium findings. The shell-pattern
  and unpinned-action findings are gone. The three remaining high findings are
  the repeated `model.eval()` false positive. The catalog gate is not cleared.

CLI changes and tests live in `/Users/arach/dev/lattices`; workflow and review
changes live in `/Users/arach/dev/lattices-design`. Existing work in both
checkouts was preserved. These changes have not been committed or published.

## Limits

The report includes `SCAN_RESOURCE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` for
`action-record-the-work.mp4` (16 MiB file limit). It has no specific hardcoded-secret
or approval-bypass finding. Incomplete category checks must not be reported as
either confirmed vulnerabilities or clean results. Cisco deep scanning was also
unavailable. No suppression or exclusion was added to improve the score.

The model evaluation false positive does not audit model loading:
`trust_remote_code=True` is a separate trust boundary in that optional verification
script. This pass did not change or validate its remote model dependencies.

Hosted workflows remain manual. Local validation does not prove a signed release
or hosted deployment succeeds. No catalog comment, scan rerun, release, or
publication is part of this source-hardening change.
